evals.prompt: We're a platform team standing up an Internal Developer Platform on Amazon EKS so our app teams can self-serve. Lay out the reference architecture and the opinionated tool stack: what runs where, how clusters are organized, and how a developer goes from idea to running service. We don't want to manage nodes and we want GitOps end to end.
expectations: Recommends a hub-and-spoke topology (hub for the platform control plane, spokes for workloads).
Recommends EKS Auto Mode for the hub-and-spoke topology.
Names Backstage as the developer portal/self-service front door.
Names ArgoCD as the GitOps CD engine.
Describes the end-to-end self-service flow: Backstage template to Git to ArgoCD sync to controller reconciliation (kro/ACK, or KubeVela/ACK).
Identifies that EKS Auto Mode removes node management, matching the 'we don't want to manage nodes' requirement.
Covers identity (Keycloak SSO).
Covers credential-free workload IAM (EKS Pod Identity / IRSA).

knowledge_assertions.context: Must recommend hub-and-spoke cluster topology as the default architecture
Must recommend EKS Auto Mode as the default cluster type for zero node management
Backstage is the opinionated developer portal choice in this stack
ArgoCD is the opinionated GitOps CD engine in this stack
Keycloak provides SSO/OIDC across all platform tools
Kargo is the multi-stage promotion tool in the opinionated stack
ACK provides self-service AWS resource provisioning as Kubernetes CRDs
The GitOps Bridge pattern connects infrastructure metadata to clusters
Workload IAM should use Pod Identity or IRSA for credential-free access
The application model layer uses kro by default, or KubeVela/OAM, for developer-facing abstractions

evals.prompt: I want a golden path for app teams on our EKS platform: a developer should only provide a Dockerfile and a simple app definition, then get a CI/CD pipeline and a safe rollout to dev and prod. Walk me through how to design this: the developer contract, how the pipeline is provisioned, how the app is described without raw Kubernetes YAML, and how we promote to prod safely.
expectations: Defines a narrow developer contract: the developer provides a Dockerfile and the platform's application manifest (a kro-rendered resource by default, or an OAM Application on the KubeVela alternative).
States that the platform handles the rest.
Uses a Backstage template that provisions the pipeline.
Provisions the pipeline via a kro CICDPipeline.
Uses Argo Workflows for CI in the pipeline.
Uses ArgoCD for CD in the pipeline.
Explains the app is described through the platform abstraction (kro by default, or OAM/KubeVela Components and Traits) rather than raw Kubernetes manifests.
Specifies Argo Rollouts canary.
Specifies quality gates (functional, performance, and/or metrics) for the canary.
Specifies that the quality gates auto-rollback on failure.
Uses Kargo for multi-stage promotion.
Uses multi-stage promotion of the same validated artifact.
Kargo auto-promotes to dev.
Kargo requires manual approval to promote to prod.

knowledge_assertions.context: Backstage templates are the front door for the golden path
Argo Workflows provides the CI pipeline in the golden path
Progressive delivery uses Argo Rollouts canary strategy with quality gates
Canary rollout must include quality gates (functional/performance/metrics)
Quality gates trigger automatic rollback on failure
Kargo orchestrates multi-stage promotion from dev to prod
Prod promotion requires manual approval while dev is auto-promoted
kro composes the CI/CD pipeline as a single CRD (CICDPipeline)
